decisions.text: type bar: the parts overlap: a plain bar chart (the book's tree); better, D-24 (b), make them disjoint in the data (Other cars = Cars − Sports cars) or stack each parent from its sub-parts (G0.14)
nominal categories sorted by value, descending
every name fits under its bar, neighbours at least 10 pt apart: vertical bars
5 values against 8 scale labels: whichever puts fewer numbers on the chart (G2.18): the values labelled directly, the value scale and its gridlines removed, the zero line kept as the baseline
value labels as a set, one magnitude and one number of decimals, the prefix and suffix on each: $118 million, $62 million, $37 million, $21 million, $20 million (G6.16, G7.4)
every label just outside its bar's end: neither the text grey nor white reads on the bar's colour at 4.5 : 1 (G7.4, G6.5)
the unit's description on its own line above the plot: “sales”; the labels carry its prefix, suffix and magnitude

source.shows: categories that contain one another (sports cars within cars): the overlap check fails, so a plain bar chart, as the book's tree gives (R7-05, G0.14); the better answer, the parts made disjoint in the data (D-24 (b)), is P3-07
